item.research_question: Can shear band-driven precipitate dispersion be used to create ultrastrong ductile medium-entropy alloys?
item.processing_route: Cold-rolling and subsequent heat treatment at 800, 850, and 900 °C for 1 h
key_findings: The A800 alloy exhibits a yield strength of 1500 MPa and an ultimate tensile strength of 1727 MPa
The A850 alloy shows a remarkable strength-ductility balance of 1587 MPa × 26.7%
The L21 precipitates have a semicoherent interface with the disordered FCC matrix
The micro-shear bands act as heterogeneous nucleation sites for the L21 precipitates
The intragranular L21 precipitates contribute to the strengthening through the Orowan bowing mechanism
item.mechanism: The shear band-driven precipitate dispersion leads to the formation of semicoherent nanoprecipitates, which enhances the strength and ductility of the alloy
item.limitations: The limited process windows in conventional processing restrict the refinement of grains to sizes smaller than ~2 μm
item.future_work: Further investigation of the deformation mechanism and the effect of processing parameters on the microstructure and properties of the alloy
quotes: shear band-driven dispersion of nano-sized and semicoherent precipitates
the L21 Heusler phase exhibits a high degree of coherency with the disordered BCC matrix

records.text: Paper card. Question: Can shear band-driven precipitate dispersion be used to create ultrastrong ductile medium-entropy alloys?. System: Al0.2CoNiV medium-entropy alloy. Processing: Cold-rolling and subsequent heat treatment at 800, 850, and 900 °C for 1 h. Test conditions: Room-temperature tensile tests. Findings: The A800 alloy exhibits a yield strength of 1500 MPa and an ultimate tensile strength of 1727 MPa; The A850 alloy shows a remarkable strength-ductility balance of 1587 MPa × 26.7%; The L21 precipitates have a semicoherent interface with the disordered FCC matrix; The micro-shear bands act as heterogeneous nucleation sites for the L21 precipitates; The intragranular L21 precipitates contribute to the strengthening through the Orowan bowing mechanism. Mechanism: The shear band-driven precipitate dispersion leads to the formation of semicoherent nanoprecipitates, which enhances the strength and ductility of the alloy. Limitations: The limited process windows in conventional processing restrict the refinement of grains to sizes smaller than ~2 μm. Future work: Further investigation of the deformation mechanism and the effect of processing parameters on the microstructure and properties of the alloy. Quote: "shear band-driven dispersion of nano-sized and semicoherent precipitates"
